title: HOLD: restore git-source-extract.ts to task-77207fb3's plan scope once task-d85fd8fd has landed
description:
BOOKKEEPING ROW, filed 2026-09-09 by architect-f04f69cf under the governor's instruction on task-d85fd8fd (reopenReason, owner "do whats needed"): "file a HOLD row to restore its scope after this row lands, exactly as task-b58778da does for controlled-3." It exists so a deliberate temporary narrowing does not become a permanent silent one.

WHAT WAS NARROWED, AND WHY. task-77207fb327a9462b869ff647650e57cf's plan reserved `apps/daemon/src/repository/git-source-extract.ts` in the affectedFiles of its step 1 and step 3. That file is UPSTREAM task-d85fd8fd's OWN untracked deliverable. The result was a reservation cycle: the downstream plan's claim made upstream's completion commit skip the contested path, so upstream could not land; upstream not landing meant the downstream's dependsOn never cleared, so the downstream never started, so the reservation was never released. Neither row could move.

I removed that one path from those two steps and resubmitted the plan. Nothing else changed - the DoD, dependsOn and every step description are verbatim, and step 3 gained a scope note telling its worker to confirm this restoration before executing item 2 (the bare-repo fold, which genuinely edits the helper).

MECHANISM, DECLARED because it differs from the governor's wording. They named `moe.amend_plan_step`; that tool takes only `description` and has no `affectedFiles` parameter, so it cannot narrow a file claim. `moe.submit_plan` can, and requires PLANNING, so task-77207fb3 was hopped WORKING -> PLANNING first. The hop cost nothing: the row was 0/5 with every step PENDING and unassigned, so no completed work, step note or evidence existed to lose. No direct `.moe` write was made.

WHAT THIS ROW DOES. Once task-d85fd8fd is DONE and `git-source-extract.ts` is TRACKED at HEAD, put that path back into task-77207fb3's step 1 and step 3 affectedFiles, and delete step 3's scope note since it will no longer apply. That is the whole job. It is safe by then because a tracked file that upstream has landed is no longer upstream's to lose, and the downstream row legitimately owns it for the fold.

WHY IT IS NOT OPTIONAL. Without it, task-77207fb3's step 3 tells a worker to extract a shared primitive out of a file the plan does not declare. The worker either edits an undeclared path, which starts the next contest, or stops - and a row stopped by a stale scope note is worse than one that never narrowed.

PRESERVATION, and this outlives the row: while `git-source-extract.ts` and its one-line bridge `git-source-extract.js` are UNTRACKED (`??`), the working tree is their ONLY copy. `git diff` is blind to them and the wrapper skips them, so nothing will warn anyone. NEVER checkout, stash, reset or clean this checkout while that is true. A governor holds an out-of-tree rescue copy as a safety net, not a landing.
definitionOfDone: `apps/daemon/src/repository/git-source-extract.ts` is tracked at HEAD (git ls-files returns it) and task-d85fd8fd is DONE - both confirmed and quoted before any edit to task-77207fb3.
task-77207fb3's step 1 and step 3 affectedFiles each name `apps/daemon/src/repository/git-source-extract.ts` again, and its distinct-file count returns to 5.
Step 3's temporary scope note is removed, and no other step description, the DoD, or dependsOn is altered - proven by quoting the before and after of the changed fields only.

task-77207fb3 is left in a state a worker can claim, and this row's completion record names the exact tool used and why, so the next reader can tell a deliberate restoration from an accidental widening.
reopenReason: Documentary hold remains enforced while fa owns consumer772 restoration. ed42 voluntarily released this zero-step hold twice after generic reclaims; park the unassigned hold outside the architect claim pool to stop duplicate handoff churn. Do not archive/drop dependency until consumer scope restoration is complete. No implementation task, completed step, or worker claim was cleared.
